Unlock Your Investment with Property Redemption in DeKalb County, Georgia

Investing in tax deeds in DeKalb County, Georgia, lets you acquire properties at a low cost or earn high returns through strategic opportunities. This article will guide you through the process and provide you with all the essential information you need to start.

Why DeKalb County, Georgia?

DeKalb County is a great place for property investment and tax deed investing because of its strong economy and variety of properties. With a population of about 750,000, the county offers a rich culture, solid economic health, and nice weather, making it a great choice for investors.

DeKalb County Tax Sales Information

Click Here to Book a Call with Dustin Hahn

How Tax Deed Sales Work in DeKalb County

  • Schedule: Tax sales are usually held from April through December on the first Tuesday of each month at the DeKalb County Courthouse steps.
  • Notice: Sales are advertised in The Champion Newspaper once a week for four weeks before the sale.
  • Bidding: Bidding starts with the total of taxes and costs on each parcel. The highest bidder gets a tax deed but doesn’t get immediate control over the property.
  • Redemption Period: The property owner has 12 months to reclaim the property by paying the redemption price, which includes the sale amount, extra taxes, and a 20% premium for the first year. This premium goes up by 10% each additional year​​.

Steps to Start Tax Deed Investing in Dekalb County

Research Local Laws: Learn the rules and laws in DeKalb County.

Visit the Treasurer’s Website: Get tax sale info on the DeKalb Tax Commissioner’s website.

Check the Auction Site: Auctions happen at the DeKalb County Courthouse steps.

Read the Details: Know the sale schedule and other important details.

Contact the County Office: For more info, contact the Tax Commissioner’s office at 404-298-4000 or email delinquentcollections2@dekalbtax.org.

Pro Tips

  • Use ‘Defeasible Titles’: Even if you don’t get immediate ownership, the high returns make it worth it. Investors can earn a 20% return in the first year, increasing to 50% in later years.
  • Do Your Homework: Always check the tax history of the property on the DeKalb County Tax Commissioner’s website before buying.

FAQs

Q: What happens if the property is reclaimed?

A: The original owner can reclaim the property within 12 months by paying the redemption price, which includes the sale amount and a 20% premium for the first year, plus an extra 10% for each following year.

Q: How can I join a tax deed auction?

A: Register on the DeKalb County Tax Commissioner’s website and go to the auction at the DeKalb County Courthouse steps.
